cities.base: Sultanahmet or, better, Sirkeci and Cagaloglu just north of it. You are ten minutes on foot from Hagia Sophia, Topkapi and the cistern, on the T1 tram line, and one Golden Horn bridge from dinner in K
cities.name: Istanbul: the historic peninsula

cities.base: Karakoy or Galata, on the slope between the ferry piers and the tower. Restaurants, bars, the Modern and the hamam are within a 15 minute walk, the funicular and tram carry you to the old city in ten
cities.name: Istanbul: Galata, Beyoglu and the Golden Horn

cities.base: You do not sleep here on a ten day trip; you arrive by ferry from Eminonu or Karakoy for 20 minutes and half a dollar, eat, walk Moda, and take a boat back. It is where Istanbul is least performed for
cities.name: Kadikoy and the Asian shore

cities.base: Goreme village itself if you want to walk to the valleys, the balloon pickups and dinner; Uchisar or Ortahisar if you want quiet and a view and do not mind driving for every meal. A cave room is worth
cities.name: Goreme, Cappadocia

cities.base: Selcuk town, not Kusadasi. It is a 12 minute drive from the Ephesus gates, has the museum and the St John hill inside the town, family pensions rather than resorts, and no cruise ship street. Kusadasi
cities.name: Selcuk

cities.base: Nobody sleeps at Ephesus. You come from Selcuk, 4 km away, and the move that decides the day is taking a taxi to the Upper Gate at 08:00 and walking downhill to the Lower Gate, so you are ahead of the
cities.name: Ephesus

places.name: Hagia Sophia
places.note: Foreigners pay 25 euro and enter by the northeast door for the upper gallery, because the ground floor is kept for prayer. It shuts to visitors around prayer times and for roughly 12:00 to 14:30 on Fridays, so do not build a Friday midday around it.

places.name: Topkapi Palace and the Harem
places.note: Closed Tuesdays, and the ticket office shuts at 17:00. The combined ticket at 2,750 lira covers the palace, the Harem and Hagia Irene; the basic ticket does not include the Harem, which is the half worth seeing.

places.name: Basilica Cistern
places.note: 1,950 lira by day and 3,000 lira after 19:30 for the same columns with more theatre lighting. Forty five minutes is plenty and the queue at 09:00 is a third of what it is at noon.

places.name: Blue Mosque (Sultanahmet Camii)
places.note: Free, working mosque, shut to visitors for about 90 minutes around each of the five prayers and all Friday midday. The tiles that give it the name are up in the gallery and you cannot get close to them.

places.name: Suleymaniye Mosque
places.note: Sinan's best building in the city and free, with a terrace over the Golden Horn behind it. Quieter than Sultanahmet because it is a 15 minute uphill walk from the tram.

places.name: Istanbul Archaeological Museums
places.note: Three buildings, 15 euro, and the Alexander Sarcophagus alone justifies it. Winter hours drop to 17:00 and last entry is 45 minutes before close. The best rain plan in Sultanahmet.

places.name: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
places.note: Carpets, Qurans and Ottoman woodwork inside Ibrahim Pasha's palace on the Hippodrome, 17 euro. Open 08:30 to 17:30 from November and 10:00 to 20:00 in summer; indoors, never crowded, 20 metres from the Blue Mosque queue.

places.name: Grand Bazaar
places.note: Shut all day Sunday and on religious holidays. Go for the covered streets and the old han courtyards off the edges, not the bargains, which are not bargains.

places.name: Spice Bazaar (Misir Carsisi)
places.note: Skip the hall itself, which is now saffron at four times the price and men shouting about Turkish viagra. The working market is the Tahtakale streets immediately west of it, where the city actually buys its coffee, cheese and nuts.

places.name: Kuru Fasulyeci Erzincanli Ali Baba
places.note: White beans in copper pots, rice, pickles, one glass of ayran, eaten at a folding table outside the Suleymaniye walls with students and taxi drivers. Lunch only in practice, and the queue moves fast.

places.name: Hamdi Restaurant
places.note: Southeastern kebab done properly, with a rooftop looking at the Galata Bridge and the Suleymaniye. Book the terrace and be specific about it, because the lower floors have no view and the same prices.

places.name: Cemberlitas Hamami
places.note: A Sinan bath from 1584, separate sections for men and women, around 60 to 75 dollars for the scrub and foam wash. Touristy and still the right thing to do on a cold wet evening. Book the slot online, prices rise every season.

places.name: Galata Tower
places.note: Thirty euro to queue 40 minutes for a narrow balcony you shuffle around. The same view is free from the terrace bars on Serdar-i Ekrem or from the Karakoy ferry, and the tower looks better from outside than from inside.

places.name: Istanbul Modern
places.note: Renzo Piano building on the Bosphorus, 900 lira, closed Mondays and opens at 11:00 on Sundays. The rooftop terrace and the reflecting pool are worth as much as the collection. Good in rain.

places.name: Pera Museum
places.note: Small, about 300 lira, closed Mondays, and it holds Osman Hamdi Bey's Tortoise Trainer. Open 10:00 to 19:00, Fridays to 22:00, but Sundays only 12:00 to 18:00; an hour indoors when Istiklal is wet.

places.name: Galata Mevlevi Lodge Museum
places.note: The real dervish lodge with its octagonal wooden sema hall and the tombstones outside: 7 euro, 09:00 to 18:30 with the ticket office shut at 17:30, closed Mondays. Sema ceremonies run some weekends on a moving schedule, so confirm on the day.

places.name: Istiklal Caddesi and the nostalgic tram
places.note: Chain shops and a red tram you will not get a seat on, but the value is in the side streets: Cukurcuma for antiques, Asmalimescit for meyhanes, the Cite de Pera arcade. Walk it once at night, then leave it.

places.name: Balat and Fener on foot
places.note: Painted houses, the red brick Greek school, Ottoman synagogues, and coffee places that have multiplied since Instagram found the stairs on Kiremit Caddesi. Steep, cobbled, and best before 11:00.

places.name: Kariye Mosque (Chora)
places.note: The best Byzantine mosaics and frescoes anywhere, 20 euro, and shut to visitors on Fridays since it went back to being a mosque, though one 2026 hours list shows it open daily, so check. Cover shoulders, knees and hair; Balat is a 20 minute walk downhill.

places.name: Karakoy Gulluoglu
places.note: Pay at the till first, then carry the receipt to the counter and ask for pistachio kuru baklava. Standing room, paper plates, open from breakfast. The branches elsewhere in the city are not the same company.

places.name: Mandabatmaz
places.note: A shopfront in an alley off Istiklal that makes one thing, Turkish coffee thick enough to hold the foam. Four stools inside, plastic chairs outside, two dollars. Say orta unless you want it sweet.

places.name: Asmali Cavit
places.note: An old-school meyhane: the cold meze tray comes to the table, you point, and then raki and fried liver for three hours. Small, so reserve, and expect the meyhanes on this street to be dark on Sundays.

places.name: Kilic Ali Pasa Hamami
places.note: Another Sinan bath, restored for seven years and the better building of the two, around 80 dollars. Men and women use it at different times of day rather than in different rooms, so check your slot when you book.

places.name: The long Bosphorus ferry to Anadolu Kavagi
places.note: The Sehir Hatlari public boat, not a tour: 10:35 from Eminonu, Besiktas, Uskudar, Kanlica, Sariyer, Rumeli Kavagi, into Anadolu Kavagi at 12:25, back out at 15:00. You are stuck in the village for over two hours, which is the flaw. Sit on the right going up.

places.name: Ciya Sofrasi
places.note: Musa Dagdeviren cooks regional Anatolian dishes that Istanbul restaurants do not: sour kebabs, wild herbs, stuffed things by weight. You choose from the steam table and pay by the kilo, so a big plate can surprise you.

places.name: Kadikoy carsi
places.note: Six blocks of fishmongers, pickle shops, coffee roasters and cheese counters between the ferry pier and Bahariye. Open daily, busiest late afternoon. This is where you buy food to take home, not the Spice Bazaar.

places.name: Kadikoy Sali Pazari
places.note: The covered neighbourhood market, Tuesdays and Fridays only, produce downstairs and clothes upstairs. No English, no souvenirs, and the best tomatoes you will eat on the trip. Go before 11:00.

places.name: Fazil Bey'in Turk Kahvesi
places.note: Roasting and grinding on site since the 1920s, mastic coffee alongside the plain. Tiny tables, fast turnover, two dollars a cup. Buy beans at the counter on the way out.

places.name: Baylan Pastanesi
places.note: A 1923 patisserie with a back garden, and one thing to order: Kup Griye, caramel and croquant over ice cream. Waiters in white jackets who have worked there longer than you have been travelling.

places.name: Moda seafront walk
places.note: Flat path from Moda pier around the headland to Fenerbahce, with tea gardens, dogs, and the old island ferry terminal on the point. Sunset here faces the historic skyline across the water.

places.name: Kadife Sokak
places.note: Kadikoy's bar street, known to everyone as Barlar Sokagi, with live rock and the cheapest efes on either shore. Students, not tourists. The last ferry back to Karakoy is around midnight; after that it is a long taxi over the bridge.

places.name: Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, Uskudar
places.note: Sinan again, right at the Uskudar ferry ramp, so you can see it in the gap between two boats. Free, working, and closed to visitors around prayers.

places.name: Kuzguncuk and Icadiye Caddesi
places.note: One street of wooden houses with a synagogue, a church and a mosque within 200 metres, and a market garden at the top. Fifteen minutes by bus north of Uskudar. Half the shops shut on Monday.

places.name: Maiden's Tower (Kiz Kulesi)
places.note: Twenty seven euro for a short boat, a stairwell and a cafe on a rock. Walk the Salacak shore instead and look at it from 300 metres away, which is the only angle that ever made it famous.

places.name: Sunrise balloon flight over Goreme
places.note: Pickup 60 to 90 minutes before sunrise, roughly an hour in the air, back by breakfast. From about 150 euro standard and well over 250 for a small basket. The civil aviation authority cancels on wind, so book the first of your mornings and keep the others free.

places.name: Goreme Open Air Museum
places.note: Ten rock-cut churches in one bowl, 20 euro, open daily. Be there at 08:00 or after 15:00; between those it is tour coaches and heat. The Museum Pass Turkiye covers it.

places.name: Karanlik Kilise (the Dark Church)
places.note: A separate 6 euro ticket inside the museum and the only one that matters: almost no light reached these frescoes for centuries, so the blues are still blue. Twenty minutes, no photography, worth the surcharge.

places.name: Uchisar Castle
places.note: The highest rock in Cappadocia, about 9 euro, not on the Museum Pass, 08:00 to 17:00 in winter and to 20:00 in summer on a secondary list, so check. Steep exposed steps; late afternoon beats sunrise because you look east over the valleys.

places.name: Pigeon Valley walk
places.note: Free, 4 km downhill from Uchisar into Goreme, past dovecotes cut into the cliffs that farmers built for fertiliser. The path braids and is muddy after rain, but you cannot really get lost with Uchisar rock behind you.

places.name: Red Valley and Rose Valley at sunset
places.note: Two valleys that share a ridge and a small entrance fee at the road end. Walk in from Cavusin and out at the Kizilcukur viewpoint; the rock goes orange for about 25 minutes and then everyone drives away at once.

places.name: Zelve Open Air Museum
places.note: Three valleys of cave dwellings lived in until 1952, about 12 euro, far emptier than Goreme, and the ticket covers Pasabag's mushroom rocks too. Hours vary, check: a reseller lists 08:00 to 19:00, likely shorter in winter. Bring a torch.

places.name: Kaymakli Underground City
places.note: About 13 euro, 40 minutes south of Goreme, four levels of stables, churches and air shafts, 08:00 to 17:00 in winter and to 19:00 in summer. Seven to ten degrees all year and low ceilings; the obvious rain plan, no good if you dislike crawling.

places.name: Turasan Winery
places.note: Cellars cut into the tufa in Urgup, tasting flights of Emir and Okuzgozu for a few dollars. Cappadocian whites are sharp and dry and travel badly, which is why you have not had them at home.

places.name: Topdeck Cave Restaurant
places.note: A family kitchen in a cave house on Hafiz Abdullah Efendi Sokak, maybe eight tables, mezes then a slow-cooked main. Reserve a day ahead in season or you will not get in. No alcohol licence some seasons, so ask.

places.name: Seten Restaurant
places.note: The most serious cooking in Goreme village, Anatolian dishes plated carefully, a proper list of Turkish wine, terrace above the town. Costs twice what the pension restaurants charge and is worth it once.

places.name: Sunset ATV tour
places.note: Forty quad bikes in convoy through Love Valley in a dust cloud, chewing up the same soft rock everyone came to look at. Walk the valleys instead; you will see more and hear something other than two-stroke engines.

places.name: Ephesus Archaeological Museum
places.note: Ten euro, and it holds everything portable that was dug out of the ruins, including the two Artemis statues covered in what may or may not be bull testicles. Do the site first, then this, not the other way round. Air conditioned.

places.name: Basilica of St John
places.note: Justinian's ruined basilica over what tradition holds is the apostle's grave, 6 euro, on the hill above the town. Marble, storks nesting on the columns, and a clear view down to the Isa Bey mosque and the one Artemis column.

places.name: Isa Bey Mosque
places.note: A 1375 Seljuk mosque built from Ephesus columns, free, and the courtyard is usually empty. Hours vary, check: roughly 08:00 to sunset, shut during prayers and Friday midday, so cover up and take shoes off.

places.name: Ayasoluk Fortress
places.note: Byzantine and Seljuk walls at the top of the same hill, entered on the St John ticket, so walk up rather than paying twice. Exposed and shadeless; not a July midday plan.

places.name: Temple of Artemis
places.note: One re-erected column in a marshy field with a stork on top, and that is the whole of a wonder of the ancient world. Free and on the road between the museum and the mosque, so look at it for five minutes; do not plan around it.

places.name: Selcuk Saturday market
places.note: Saturdays only, filling the streets behind the bus station with village produce, cheese, olives and dried figs from the surrounding hills. If your Selcuk nights do not include a Friday, you will miss it.

places.name: Sirince village
places.note: A Greek hill village 8 km up a switchback road, minibuses every half hour from Selcuk otogar. The fruit wine is sweet and mostly a souvenir. Come before 11:00, because the coach parties own it from then until four.

places.name: Pamucak Beach
places.note: Eight kilometres of undeveloped grey sand at the mouth of the Kucuk Menderes, 15 minutes west of town, free and often nearly empty. The water shelves slowly and the wind gets up in the afternoon. No shade, few facilities.

places.name: Mehmet and Ali Baba Kebab House
places.note: A small street kitchen off Ataturk Caddesi that has fed backpackers for 20 years: grilled meat, meze, free tea, owners who will talk to you all night. Cash is easiest.

places.name: Ejder Restaurant
places.note: On the pedestrian street under the aqueduct where the storks nest, doing home-style Aegean dishes and wood-fired things. Sit outside in the evening and watch the birds come back to the arches.

places.name: Library of Celsus
places.note: The 40 euro site ticket is paid once at the gate and covers everything here except the Terrace Houses. The facade is a 1970s reassembly of original stone and it still stops people walking. Empty at 08:00, three coach loads deep by 10:00.

places.name: The Terrace Houses
places.note: A separate 15 euro ticket for the covered hillside insulae: mosaic floors, painted walls, plumbing, six houses of rich Ephesians under a roof. The best hour on the site and the one most people skip to save money. Shaded, so good at noon.

places.name: The Great Theatre
places.note: Twenty five thousand seats cut into Panayir hill, inside the site ticket so no charge on top, 08:00 to 18:00 with last tickets 17:30 in winter. Climbing is limited to the lower tiers, and the acoustics demonstration at the bottom runs about every four minutes in season.

places.name: Curetes Street
places.note: The marble slope from the upper gate down to the library, lined with column bases, shop fronts and the odd mosaic pavement. Polished stone, uneven, and genuinely slippery in normal shoes when wet.

places.name: Temple of Hadrian
places.note: The small arched facade halfway down Curetes Street with Tyche over the door, no charge beyond the site ticket. The reliefs in place are casts; the originals are in the Selcuk museum, which is the argument for doing both in one day.

places.name: The Odeon and the Upper Agora
places.note: Where you come in if you take a taxi to the Magnesia Gate at 08:00 and walk down: a 1,500 seat council chamber and the civic square, seen while you are fresh and it is cool. No charge beyond the site ticket.

places.name: The public latrines
places.note: A marble bench with holes in it, a drain beneath, and a room where the city did its business in company; no charge beyond the site ticket. Ten minutes, and it tells you more about Roman daily life than the library does.

places.name: Church of Mary
places.note: The council church of 431 near the lower gate, low walls and brick apses, usually empty because it is 200 metres off the main route. Worth the detour on the way out if the heat has not finished you.

places.name: House of the Virgin Mary (Meryem Ana Evi)
places.note: A small stone chapel 7 km up the mountain, 700 lira, reached only by taxi or tour. A pilgrimage site rather than a ruin, and queues of 30 minutes are normal. Quiet woods, and no queue at all in the last hour.

places.name: Pandeli
places.note: Ottoman-era lokanta upstairs at the Spice Bazaar entrance, on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list since the first Istanbul selection. Lunch and early dinner, 11:30 to 19:00, closed Sundays; about 700 lira a head on average (range 400 to 1,200, Jun 2026).

places.name: Giritli
places.note: Cretan meze in a Sultanahmet villa with outdoor tables: a 50 euro set of 20 meze, a main and unlimited drinks, or about 1,800 lira a head a la carte (Jun 2026). Bib Gourmand 2026, 13:00 to midnight daily, book on +90 212 458 22 70.

places.name: Hagia Irene
places.note: The oldest surviving church in Istanbul, a mosaic cross in its bare apse and acoustics good enough for concerts. Closed Tuesdays, 09:00 to 16:45 in winter (18:45 summer), 1,050 lira alone or inside the 2,750 lira Topkapi combined ticket.

places.name: Little Hagia Sophia (Kucuk Ayasofya)
places.note: Justinian's 6th century church, now a working mosque and the prototype for Hagia Sophia up the hill. Hours unknown, so check the price and avoid prayer times; 30 minutes is enough.

places.name: Rustem Pasha Mosque
places.note: A Sinan mosque faced in Iznik tiles, reopened in 2021 after restoration, a few minutes from the Spice Bazaar. Should be free as a working mosque, though not verified; hours unknown, so avoid prayer times.

places.name: Hippodrome of Constantinople (Sultanahmet Square)
places.note: The chariot track of Byzantine Constantinople, now a square, with the Obelisk of Theodosius, the Serpent Column and the Walled Obelisk still in line along it. Free and open all hours; 30 minutes between Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque.

places.name: Column of Constantine (Cemberlitas)
places.note: The column Constantine dedicated in 330 AD for his new capital, standing on the tram line at Cemberlitas. Free, open air, fifteen minutes on the walk to the Grand Bazaar.

places.name: Aheste
places.note: Modern meze in Pera, on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list, dinner only from 18:00 to midnight. About 900 lira a head on average (range 600 to 1,400, Jun 2026); book for a weekend.

places.name: Hayvore
places.note: Black Sea and Anatolian cooking a few steps off Istiklal, open 09:00 to midnight, so it works for lunch between Pera and Galata. About 700 lira a head on average (range 400 to 1,200, Jun 2026).

places.name: Dolmabahce Palace
places.note: The last residence of the Ottoman sultans, 2,000 lira, 09:00 to 18:00 with last entry 17:00, closed Mondays, 1 January and the first day of religious holidays. There is a daily visitor cap, so book ahead and go early.

places.name: Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisari)
places.note: Mehmed II built it in four months in 1452 to close the Bosphorus before the conquest. 6 euro, closed Mondays, 09:00 to 18:30 in winter and 19:30 in summer, last entry an hour before closing.

places.name: Ortakoy Mosque
places.note: A baroque mosque on the water directly under the Bosphorus Bridge, free to enter. Hours are not published, so avoid prayer times; thirty minutes is enough.

places.name: Pammakaristos Church (Fethiye Museum)
places.note: A Byzantine side chapel in Fener with Palaiologan mosaics and none of the Chora crowd. Tickets are sold at the chapel itself, so check the price and the hours; forty minutes, easy to add to a Balat morning.

places.name: Galata Bridge
places.note: Fishermen along the rails on top and restaurants on the lower deck, walked from Karakoy to Eminonu. Free and always open; 25 minutes on foot to the old city.

places.name: Pumpkin Goreme Restaurant
places.note: A restaurant that doubles as an art gallery, dinner only 18:00 to 23:00, 4.7 on 891 Google reviews. The price is a midpoint of mains at $7 to 25 on a Jan 2026 guide, starters $6 to 8, so the full bill runs higher.

places.name: Nazar Borek & Cafe
places.note: Family-run gozleme and borek cafe, 12:00 to 22:00, closed Mondays, 4.8 on 1,512 Google reviews. Mains $6 to 10 on a Jan 2026 guide (main course only), so a cheap lunch between valley walks.

places.name: CANCAN Cafe and Restaurant
places.note: Casual Turkish cooking from 09:00 to 23:00 daily, 4.8 on 2,419 Google reviews. Mains $6 to 10 on a Jan 2026 guide, which is the main course only, not the whole bill.

places.name: Aysel'in Mutfagi
places.note: Home-style Anatolian cooking, 4.5 on 3,302 Google reviews. Hours vary, check; mains $8 to 20 on a Jan 2026 guide, main course only, so budget a little more.

places.name: Sunset and Sunrise Balloon Viewpoint
places.note: The hill above the village for watching the balloons go up at sunrise and the town at sunset, 4.7 on 2,518 Google reviews. Open all hours; reviewers mention a 30 to 60 lira entry, undated.

places.name: Love Valley
places.note: Tall tuff pillars with old monastic cave rooms cut into them, free and open all hours. Allow 90 minutes on foot.

places.name: Sword Valley
places.note: A free valley with cave dwellings in its walls and no ticket needed. The ATV convoys come through later in the day, so go early and allow 90 minutes.

places.name: Yusuf Koc Church
places.note: A small rock-cut church reached by a 13-step iron ladder, with few visitors. It may be on private land with a charge, so check the price; hours unknown, 30 minutes.

places.name: Cavusin old village
places.note: An abandoned cave village on the cliff above Cavusin, with two rock-cut churches of St John the Baptist. Free; give it an hour, and it is where the Red Valley walk starts.

places.name: Byzantine Aqueduct
places.note: The aqueduct that carried water from Sirince to the basin on St John's hill, now a row of arches in the town centre with storks nesting on top. Free and always open; 20 minutes.

places.name: Priene
places.note: A Hellenistic city laid out on a grid under Mount Mycale, with the Temple of Athena Polias, about 33 km south of Selcuk as the crow flies. Hours vary, check, and check the price; allow two hours plus the drive.

places.name: Miletus
places.note: The Ionian trading city, with its Roman theatre and the Baths of Faustina. 6 euro and 08:00 to 17:00 all year, but both come from an undated official page, so check; two hours plus the drive, about 48 km from Selcuk.

places.name: Temple of Apollo, Didyma
places.note: The giant Ionic oracle temple of Apollo, with the Medusa-head frieze, about 64 km from Selcuk. 6 euro on an undated official page; hours vary, check. Pair it with Miletus on one day out.

places.name: Bottarga Restaurant
places.note: Seafood and Mediterranean plates on the Kusadasi front, about 18 km from Selcuk, 16:00 to midnight daily. The price is the midpoint of a $50 to 100 a head band listed in September 2026, not a menu; winter opening is not confirmed, so call first.

outings.why: Pickup in the dark 60 to 90 minutes before sunrise, an hour airborne over Love Valley and the Goreme bowl, champagne on a trailer at the end. The hard part is not the flying, it is that the aviation authority grounds every balloon on a wind
outings.name: The sunrise balloon flight
outings.season: All year, most reliable September to October and April to Ma
outings.fallback: Drive to the Kizilcukur ridge for sunrise instead and watch from the ground, which costs a few dollars and works in any wind.

outings.why: Ten monastic churches cut into one valley, plus the 6 euro Dark Church where the frescoes survived because the light did not get in. Doors open at 08:00 and the coaches arrive at 10:00, so the whole quality of the visit depends on when you
outings.name: Goreme Open Air Museum and the Dark Church
outings.fallback: Cavusin village church and the Zelve valleys, which take the same shoes and hold a fraction of the people.

outings.why: Four kilometres of dovecote cliffs, downhill the whole way if you start at Uchisar castle and finish in Goreme for lunch. Free, unmarked in places, and greasy clay after rain.
outings.name: Pigeon Valley, Uchisar down to Goreme
outings.season: All year, avoid midday June to August
outings.fallback: Walk the paved section from the Uchisar viewpoint to the first dovecotes and turn around, 40 minutes.

outings.why: In from Cavusin, through the rose-coloured canyons and out at the Kizilcukur viewpoint for the last half hour of light. Seven kilometres, a few ladders and tunnels, and a small fee at the ridge. Take a torch, because you will finish in the
outings.name: Red Valley to Cavusin at sunset
outings.fallback: Drive straight to the Kizilcukur viewpoint car park 40 minutes before sunset and skip the walk.

outings.why: Two underground cities 40 and 55 minutes south of Goreme, 13 euro each, one wide and one deep. Ducking through 1.5 metre tunnels for an hour is not for everyone, and both cities are a poor idea if crowds underground bother you. This is the
outings.name: Kaymakli and Derinkuyu underground
outings.fallback: Kaymakli alone plus the Guzelyurt valley on the way back, three hours total.

outings.why: A green river canyon 90 minutes southwest of Goreme with rock churches along the banks, walked from the Ihlara stairs to Belisirma and on to the Selime monastery. Fifteen euro to enter, and the driving either end makes it a whole day whethe
outings.name: Ihlara Valley, Belisirma to Selime
outings.fallback: The stepped section from the main entrance down to Agacalti church and back up, two hours.

outings.why: Taxi to the Magnesia Gate at 08:00 and walk downhill through the Odeon, Curetes Street, the Terrace Houses and the theatre to the lower gate. Forty euro entry plus 15 for the Terrace Houses, no shade on most of it, and marble that is slick
outings.name: Ephesus from the Upper Gate down
outings.season: All year, brutal 12:00 to 16:00 in July and August
outings.fallback: Enter at the Lower Gate, see the theatre and library, and spend the rest of the time in the Selcuk museum.

outings.why: The chapel on Bulbul Dagi in the morning by taxi, then back down for the Basilica of St John, the fortress and the Ephesus museum on foot. Half the day is a pilgrimage site that some people find moving and others find is a small stone room
outings.name: Meryem Ana and the Selcuk hill
outings.fallback: Drop the chapel and do the St John hill, Isa Bey mosque and museum in three hours.

outings.why: Minibus from Selcuk otogar up 8 km of switchbacks to a Greek village of stone houses, then lunch and a tasting. Go at 09:00; from 11:00 to 16:00 the coach parties from the cruise port fill the single lane of shops.
outings.name: Sirince and the fruit wine houses
outings.fallback: Selcuk Saturday market and the aqueduct storks, which cost nothing and need no bus.

outings.why: Hagia Sophia at 09:00, Topkapi and the Harem before lunch, the cistern and the Blue Mosque after. Around 130 dollars a head in entry fees now, and it collapses on a Tuesday when Topkapi is shut or a Friday midday when the mosques close.
outings.name: The Sultanahmet monuments in one day
outings.fallback: The Archaeological Museums and the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts, both indoors and both a tenth as crowded.

outings.why: The public Sehir Hatlari boat leaves Eminonu at 10:35, calls at Besiktas, Uskudar, Kanlica, Sariyer and Rumeli Kavagi, and reaches the last village at 12:25. It does not leave again until 15:00, so you get a fish lunch and a castle climb wh
outings.name: The long Bosphorus ferry to Anadolu Kavagi
outings.season: All year, cold and wet on deck December to March
outings.fallback: Ride the commuter ferry Eminonu to Kadikoy and back for under a dollar, 40 minutes, same water.

outings.why: Taxi or T5 tram up the Golden Horn, the Chora mosaics first at 09:00, then downhill through Edirnekapi into the painted streets of Balat for lunch. Chora is closed to visitors all day Friday, which kills the plan.
outings.name: Balat, Fener and Kariye
outings.fallback: Balat and Fener alone on foot from Eminonu along the shore road, two and a half hours.

outings.why: Ferry across at 11:00, the market streets and lunch at Ciya, coffee at Fazil Bey, the Moda shore at sunset and bars on Kadife Sokak after. The only hard part is remembering the last boat back is around midnight.
outings.name: Crossing to Kadikoy for the day
outings.fallback: Uskudar instead, ten minutes by boat, for the Mihrimah mosque and the Salacak waterfront.

destination.name: Turkey: Istanbul, Cappadocia and Ephesus
destination.pitch: Ten days buys you one of the great cities on earth, a week's worth of rock valleys you walk rather than photograph from a bus, and the best-excavated Roman city in the Mediterranean, at the cost of two domestic flights and a museum bill tha
destination.caveat: Entry fees for foreigners are now priced in euros and are steep, 25 for Hagia Sophia and 40 for Ephesus, and the fixed closed days bite hard: Topkapi on Tuesday, Chora on Friday, the Grand Bazaar on Sunday, half the Beyoglu museums on Monday. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Istanbul is the reason to come, and four nights is the minimum that lets you see both shores and still eat properly.
because.food: Regional Anatolian cooking at Ciya, a dying meyhane culture in Asmalimescit, beans from a copper pot for nine dollars, and Aegean home food in Selcuk that never reaches a menu abroad.
because.nature: The Cappadocian valleys are walkable rather than viewable, and Pigeon, Red and Rose valleys are free and all downhill if you start high.
because.culture: Byzantium and the Ottomans in the same square kilometre, then a Roman city you walk down the main street of, and mosaics at Chora that are worth the trip on their own.
because.adventure: The balloon at dawn and a few hours underground at Kaymakli are as far as it goes; the valley walks are real walks but nobody would call them hard.
because.relaxation: Two Sinan hamams, cave hotel terraces at sunrise, and eight empty kilometres of sand at Pamucak, but this is a moving trip and not a still one.
because.exploration: Three regions in ten days, each unlike the others, and in Istanbul alone you can cross a continent for half a dollar and be somewhere with different food and no tour groups.
